mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-trend baseline (p > 0.05) during confirmed tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 3.5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher labor market disengagement typically precedes recessionary expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 70% of such labor-cooling events (rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly composite HOUST index falls by more than 10% from its prior month's level, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to sudden demand destruction and market uncertainty.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite a confirmed demand shock (as measured by independent confirmation in external data).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO reading above 110.0 (2017=100) while CPIAUCSL is below 260.0 indicates a supply-side imbalance favoring producers, which tends to depress near-term equity valuations and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such supply overhang events (rolling 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in monthly GDPC1 (real GDP) of at least 2% for three consecutive quarters is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as market anticipates economic weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous_quarter - 2% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during confirmed contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises by more than 15% from the prior month, it signals strong labor absorption and supports a positive S&P 20-day forward return as hiring momentum boosts market confidence.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed hiring booms.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly drop in both RSAFS (> -200 million dollars) and HOUST (> -1000 units) indicates weakening demand across credit and retail sectors, which predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such dual-demand weakness events (rolling 12 months).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling UNRATE (< 3.0%) and rising FEDFUNDS (> 4.0%), the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates higher interest rates will compress profit margins but also reduce discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during confirmed rate normalization episodes.
